passage:
A weather scientist visited school and explained that forecasts are made with models. A model uses data from air pressure, temperature, wind, and many other things.
A student asked why forecasts are sometimes wrong if computers are so powerful.
The scientist said the atmosphere is complex. Small changes can grow, and data is never complete. A forecast is not a promise; it is the best estimate from current information.
After the talk, students stopped treating wrong forecasts as simple failure.
They learned that uncertainty is not the enemy of science. It is part of honest science. Good predictions include both knowledge and limits.
